Artificial Intelligence is changing the way software is built. As an Angular developer preparing for Tech Lead opportunities, I decided to start a simple challenge: 15 minutes of AI learning every day for 15 days.
The goal isn’t to become an AI expert overnight. It’s to learn how AI can make me a more productive developer and a better technical leader.
What I Learned Today
The biggest lesson was that ChatGPT is not just a chatbot — it can be an AI pair programmer.
The quality of its response depends on the quality of the prompt.
Instead of asking:
“Create an Angular login component.”
I learned to provide context:
“Act as a Senior Angular Tech Lead.
I’m building an Employee Management System using Angular 21.
Design a scalable architecture using Signals, lazy loading, Angular Material, and explain your decisions.”
The difference in the response was significant. Instead of just generating code, ChatGPT explained architectural choices, module organization, and best practices.
Try it out
Act as an expert Senior Angular Enterprise Architect.
I am developing an Employee Management Portal. Here is my technical setup and roadmap:

• Frontend Stack: Angular (latest version)

• Backend Roadmap: Currently using a mock API, but migrating to a Java/Spring Boot REST API later.

• Core Portal Features: [e.g., employee directories, multi-step onboarding workflows, role-based access control, paginated data tables].
Your Task:

• Recommend the Best State Management Strategy: Suggest the ideal approach for Angular (e.g., Component Store, NgRx/Redux, Akita, Signals-based state, or plain RxJS BehaviorSubject Services).

• Address the Architecture Transition: Explain how the chosen approach smoothly bridges the transition from a mock API to a Java backend without rewriting the core state logic.

• Provide a Data Flow Example: Show a quick, high-level code folder structure or service blueprint showing how a feature (like “Fetch/Update Employee Profile”) should handle the mock-to-Java transition.
Keep the response highly structured, practical, and optimized for performance.
Do input this to your chatgpt and check the responses yourselves.
Key Takeaways

• Treat AI as a development partner, not a replacement for engineering judgment.

• Provide clear context, requirements, and constraints in your prompts.

• Use AI not only for writing code but also for architecture discussions, documentation, interview preparation, and code reviews.

• Always validate AI-generated output before using it in production.
My Next Step
Tomorrow, I’ll explore GitHub Copilot and understand how it complements ChatGPT in a real development workflow.
I’m documenting this journey publicly to stay consistent and hopefully help other developers who are starting their AI learning journey.
Thanks for reading!
